##### Imported cases: live to

ol resolution, and per-run approval

Every file run performs the same live check `eval validate --project` performs,
**before i
t writes anything**. It is not opt-in and there is no flag to skip\nit. A file with no deterministic `toolCall` steps asks no ques

tion and pays no
round trip.

What happens when a deterministic reference does not resolve depends on the
case:

| Case | Ou
tcome |\n| - | - |\n| Selected (enabled, and named by `--case` if you used it) | The launch **refuses before the suite is synced**
— nothing is written and nothing is billed |\n| Imported, not selected | Its claim is rewritten to `unresolved` (keeping `sourceC
aseKey`) and it is **still persisted**, so the hosted record says what MCPJam found rather than still asserting a claim about a mi
ssing tool |\n| Native, not selected | Left exactly as authored. A hand-written case never acquires an `import` block from this —
\"somebody wrote this\" and \"something converted this\" are different facts |\n\nEach target is checked on **its own** server set
. `--host` is checked against\nthat host's configured servers rather than the file's, because that is the set\nthe run connects —
validating `target.servers` would approve a tool the host\ncannot reach. A host the FILE declares uses its own `servers` list when
it\ndeclares one (those are attached to the host before launch) and the host's\nconfigured set when the field is omitted. An expl
icitly empty `servers: []`\nis a real, empty set — it clears the attachment before launch — and is\nvalidated as such, never as an
he run's target set cannot be enumerated before the suite exists\n(`--all-targets`, `--compose-*`), or a host does not report a se

rver set, or a
host pins a server the project no longer has, the launch refuses rather than
assuming the references are fine.

reated as possibly naming\nany enabled case, so an unresolved reference still refuses; the launcher\nresolves the selector itself
